searchText: <@412614104222531604> please use main for Besu Network features: 1B underway now. We're taking down ~18 supernodes, 17 will be left online. Then we trigger non-finality and put the pieces back together. We are also taking all of our hetzner arm machines offline and exiting them. Corner case in EIP-7823 quick question: does EIP-7825 (tx gas limit cap) apply to `eth_calls` too? We see at least one client implemented the 16M limit on eth_calls too, which is causing some issues. But I'm not sure if it's a bug or spec conform Repeating my question from ACD: Could I ask for dedicated CL engineers for glamsterdam scope? Same way as we did with peerdas. If you are volunteering please let me know. <@&1367819653279125645> would like to use `fusaka-devnet-4` branch for Lodestar how long can we expect the non-finality to last? wanted to test out some things it stopped an epoch or two ago 😛 bringing the supernodes back up now ^ should slowly chug back online now For clarification: - we took nodes offline - then submitted exits, waited for exits to process such that we cross 66% threshold - now we crossed the threshold and finalized - finally, we start back the offline nodes and see how long they take to catch up IMO this isn't a terribly unrealistic turn of events if such a thing happened on mainnet. ohh damn, so my checkpoint sync from unfinalized state wasn't really working lol we survived pretty good, and synced quick enough 😄 inspite of a peering issue which happened in the very beginning of 1b I would say no. `eth_call` is not a transaction, it is for invoking read operations and for just running the EVM. Clients may have limits on max gas there, but it should not be tied to the tx limit. almost all nodes are synced again after the non finality event, please check if your client hasn't yet: https://dora.fusaka-devnet-3.ethpandaops.io/

excerpts.author: parithosh
excerpts.content:
For clarification:
- we took nodes offline
- then submitted exits, waited for exits to process such that we cross 66% threshold
- now we crossed the threshold and finalized
- finally, we start back the offline nodes and see how long they take to catch up

IMO this isn't a terribly unrealistic turn of events if such a thing happened on mainnet.
